blocks.text: Chilliwack Townhomes Under $1.2 Million – Browse Listings

Chilliwack townhomes under $1.2 million give you real space for the money — something that's getting harder to find anywhere else in the Fraser Valley. This page pulls live MLS listings every day, so what you see is what's actually available right now. It's built for buyers who want a yard without the full price tag of a detached home, families upgrading from a condo, and people moving east from Surrey or Langley to stretch their budget. Filter by beds, baths, size, or build year to narrow things down, and reach out if you want to walk through a few.

parts.t: Townhome activity in Chilliwack has been steady. The under-$1.2M segment moves faster than higher-end detached, mostly because that's where the demand sits — first-time buyers, downsizers, and families relocating from pricier markets. Newer complexes with double garages and end-unit privacy tend to go quickly when priced right. Older or interior units sit longer if they're priced like the new ones. Inventory swings with the season — more listings hit the market in spring, things slow down in late fall. If you're seeing something you like, don't wait three weekends to think about it. Reach out and we'll go look.

Chilliwack has changed a lot in the last decade. What used to be a quiet farming town is now a growing part of the Fraser Valley,and townhomes are a big reason why. You get newer construction, attached garages, fenced yards, and most complexes are walking distance to a school or shopping.

The buyers who land here are usually one of three types: young families priced out of Abbotsford or Langley, retirees downsizing from a detached home but who still want their dog to have a yard, and remote workers who don't need to commute five days a week anymore. Schools are solid — both public and Christian options — and you've got Cultus Lake, the Vedder River, and the Sumas Mountain trails all within twenty minutes.

Commute is the main thing to think about. If you're driving to Surrey or Vancouver daily, Chilliwack will wear you down. But if you work from home, work locally, or only commute a couple days a week, the trade-off in space and price is hard to beat.
What to Expect at This Price Point

Under $1.2 million in Chilliwack gets you a lot of townhome. You're typically looking at 1,400 to 2,200 square feet, three bedrooms, two and a half baths, and a tandem or side-by-side garage. Most of the inventory is post-2010 construction, so you avoid the major mechanical and envelope issues that plague older complexes.

Strata fees usually run between $250 and $450 a month — what's covered varies, but most include exterior maintenance, the roof, and the contingency fund. The newer the complex, the lower the fees tend to be, since not as much has needed replacing yet. Always pull the depreciation report and last two years of strata minutes before you write an offer. That's where the real story is.
What's the difference between strata and freehold townhomes?
Most townhomes in Chilliwack are strata. You own your unit and share ownership of the common property — roof, siding, landscaping, sometimes a clubhouse.
You pay a monthly fee, and the strata handles the big stuff.
Freehold (or "bare land strata," which is close) means you own the land your unit sits on too, and you're responsible for more of the upkeep.
Freehold is rarer and usually a bit pricier, but you have more freedom.
How long does it usually take to sell a townhome in Chilliwack?
Depends on price, condition, and time of year.
A well-priced, well-presented townhome in a good complex can sell in under two weeks.
Something overpriced or in a complex with a bad reputation can sit for months.
Spring and early summer are usually fastest. November through January are usually slowest.
Pricing is the biggest lever — more than staging, more than photos.
Are strata fees worth it?
They're not really optional, so "worth it" is the wrong frame. The real question is whether the fee matches what you're getting.
A $400/month fee in a 25-year-old complex with a beat-up roof and no contingency reserve is bad.
A $400/month fee in a new complex with a healthy contingency fund is fine.
Always read the depreciation report.
Can I rent out a townhome I buy here?
Maybe. Each strata has its own rental rules, and some have caps or restrictions.
BC has rolled back some province-wide rental restrictions, but check the bylaws of any specific complex before you write an offer if rental flexibility matters.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Townhomes Under $1.2M Real Estate FAQs

parts.t: What types of townhomes can you buy under $1.2M in Chilliwack?

Under $1.2 million covers virtually all Chilliwack townhomes, including older 2- and 3-bedroom complexes in Chilliwack Proper ($420K–$575K), 3- and 4-bedroom family townhomes with double garages in Sardis, Promontory, and Garrison Crossing ($600K–$875K), and larger hillside view or golf-course townhomes in Eastern Hillsides and Promontory ($800K–$1.1M).
Where are rancher and master-on-main townhomes located in Sardis?

One-level rancher townhomes and master-on-main layouts are concentrated on flat ground in Sardis South (near Watson Road, Tyson Road, and South Sumas Road), Sardis West Vedder (near Evans Road and Wells Road), and along the Vedder Road corridor.
What is the difference between freehold and leasehold townhomes in Chilliwack?

Freehold strata townhomes give you an undivided share in fee-simple land, whereas leasehold townhomes sit on leased land (often 99-year prepaid leases on First Nations lands in Sardis). Always confirm the remaining lease term, whether the lease is fully prepaid, and which banks or credit unions finance that specific complex.
Are there 55+ gated townhome communities in Chilliwack and Sardis?
Yes. Sardis West Vedder, Sardis South, and Chilliwack Proper have several gated 55+ rancher and master-on-main townhome communities featuring clubhouses, RV parking, and single-level living.
Do new townhomes in Chilliwack under $1.1M qualify for the BC Newly Built Home PTT exemption?

Yes. Under BC's 2026 rules, eligible buyers purchasing a newly built townhome as a principal residence receive a full Property Transfer Tax exemption on purchase prices up to $1,100,000 (with a partial phase-out between $1,100,000 and $1,150,000).
Which Chilliwack neighbourhoods are best for families buying a townhome?

Families frequently choose Garrison Crossing (walkable to Cheam Leisure Centre,Vedder Elementary, Vedder Middle, and Sardis Secondary), Promontory (near Promontory Heights Elementary and Jinkerson Park), and Sardis East/South (near Sardis Park and Watson Glen Park).
What should I check in the strata documents when buying a Chilliwack townhome?

Inspect the Form B Information Certificate, the Depreciation Report (checking roof, siding, window, and driveway pavement timelines), pet and parking bylaws (especially truck length in garages and driveway aprons), and any hillside retaining-wall maintenance obligations in Promontory or Eastern Hillsides.
